body.text: ## Body 2.5ex 1.5ex Introduction[]{#introduction label="introduction"} We study quantum invariants arising from the infinite dimensional representation theory of the quantum group $U_q(sl_2)$. The family of finite dimensional representations of this quantum group at generic $q$ leads to the sequence of coloured Jones polynomials whereas the representations at roots of unity give the sequence of coloured Alexander polynomials (or ADO invariants [@ADO]). The asymptotic behaviour of these invariants is subject to important questions in low dimensional topology: the Volume Conjecture (Kashaev [@K],[@M2]) and Gukov-Manolescu's Conjecture ([@GM]) which predict geometric information that is contained in their limit with respect to the colour. Motivated by the question of the conjectured geometry contained in these invariants the second author provided a unified topological framework that encodes all coloured Jones and ADO polynomials at bounded colours by graded intersections in configuration spaces ([@Cr1], [@Cr2]). They lead to universal geometrical invariants for links ([@Cru1], [@Cru2]). These unification results opened up questions about encoding non-semisimple invariants and semi-simple invariants directly from a unified perspective. In [@CrG] the author defined a globalisation of Jones and Alexander invariants by constructing a graded intersection that is taking values in a quotient of a polynomial ring in two variables. **Main results** In this paper we address this problem at higher colours, and we want to unify coloured Jones and coloured Alexander invariants corresponding to $\mathcal{N}$ dimensional representations of $U_q(sl_2)$. Our strategy is to use quantum groups over two variables together with their braid group action directly on the infinite dimensional representation, which is given by the Verma module. We will work over the Laurent polynomial ring $\mathbb L=\mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}]$. **Question:** For a fixed level $\mathcal{N}$, which is the maximal quotient of $\mathbb L$ in which we can obtain invariants from the $\mathcal{N}$-dimensional part of the $U_q(sl_2)$-Verma module? We start from the generic braid action on the Verma module and define quantum traces on specialisations of the $\mathcal{N}$-dimensional part over certain quotient rings. We prove the following: - *Level $\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant at prime levels.* If $\mathcal{N}$ is prime, then the maximal quotient ring of $\mathbb L$ in which we get invariants from Verma modules is given by the ideal $\mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}$ (as in [\[qideal\]](#qideal){reference-type="eqref" reference="qideal"}, Corollary [9](#coro:prime){reference-type="ref" reference="coro:prime"}). The quantum trace in this quotient leads to a "Level $\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant" (for any level $\mathcal{N}$): $${\color{black} \Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \in {\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}}.$$ - *Level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant.* If $\mathcal{N}$ is not prime, then the maximal quotient ring in which we get invariants from Verma modules is given by the ideal $\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ (see [\[idealm\]](#idealm){reference-type="eqref" reference="idealm"}, Theorem [8](#thm:THEOREM){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:THEOREM"}). The intersection form in this quotient leads to a maximal invariant called "Level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant": $$\widetilde{\Omega}_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \in \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_\mathcal{N}.$$ - *Interpolation formula in the level $\mathcal{N}$ quotient ring.* The level $\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant $\Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$ is an interpolation between the coloured Jones and ADO invariants at level $\mathcal{N}$, which we compute explicitely in Theorem [10](#TINT){reference-type="ref" reference="TINT"}. 2.5ex -1.5ex Quotient rings Let us fix a natural number $\mathcal{N}\in \mathbb N$, $\mathcal{N}\geqslant 2$. ::: defn **Definition 1** (Level $\mathcal{N}$-quotient ideals). We are going to define two ideals in the ring $\mathbb L$, and work over the associated quotient rings, as follows. 1\) (Interpolation quotient ideal) Let $$\begin{equation} \label{qideal} \mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}:=\left(\varphi_\mathcal{N}(q^2)\cdot (s^2q^{-2(\mathcal{N}-1)}-1)\right) \subseteq \mathbb L=\mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \end{equation}$$ and refer to it as the "interpolation quotient ideal". 2\) (Maximal quotient ideal) Also, we define $$\begin{equation} \label{idealm} \widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_\mathcal{N}:=\left( \varphi_\mathcal{N}(q^2) \cdot (s^2 q^{-2\mathcal{N}+2} - 1)\right) \cap \prod_{\text{\scriptsize$\begin{matrix} d\mid \mathcal{N}\\ d \neq 1, \mathcal{N}\end{matrix}$}} \left(\varphi_d(q^2),\ \ \frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \right) \subseteq \mathbb L=\mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \end{equation}$$ and call it the "maximal quotient ideal". Here, $\varphi_\mathcal{N}(q)$ is the $\mathcal{N}^{th}$ cyclotomic polynomial. ::: ::: defn **Definition 2** (Quotient rings). We define the following two quotient rings of $\mathbb L$. 1\) The "interpolation ring", given by: $$\begin{equation} {\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}:=\mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \ / \ \mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}. \end{equation}$$ 2) The "maximal ring", given by $$\begin{equation} \label{qring} \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}:=\mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \ / \widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_\mathcal{N}. \end{equation}$$ ::: Note that there is the natural projection $\pi_{\mathcal{N}} : \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}} \to {{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ since $\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_\mathcal{N}\subset {\mathcal{I}}_\mathcal{N}$, and $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}} = {{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ if $\mathcal{N}$ is a prime number. 2.5ex -1.5ex Level $\mathcal{N}$ representation We are going to use the $U_q(sl_2)$ Verma module $\hat{V}$ (defined over ${\mathbb L}$), which is generated by an infinite family of vectors $\{v_0, v_1,...\}$. Using the two variable $R$-matrix associated to this quantum group given by [\[eq:Rpositive\]](#eq:Rpositive){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:Rpositive"} and [\[eq:Rnegative\]](#eq:Rnegative){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:Rnegative"}, we get a braid group action: $$\begin{equation} \hat{\rho}_n: B_n \rightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_{U_q(sl_2)}\left(\hat{V}^{\otimes n}\right). \end{equation}$$ We fix a level $\mathcal{N}$ and we want to use the $\mathcal{N}$-dimensional ${\mathbb L}$-submodule generated by the first $\mathcal{N}$ vectors of the Verma module. We refer to this module as the "$\mathcal{N}$-finite part from the Verma module". We introduce the following modules. ::: defn **Definition 3** (Quotient modules). Let us denote the above specialisations of the $\mathcal{N}$-finite part from the Verma module over the interpolation ring and over the maximal ring respectively: $$\begin{equation} \begin{aligned} & 1) \text{ Interpolation module}: \ \ \ \ \ V_{\mathcal{N}}:=\langle v_{0},...,v_{\mathcal{N}-1}\rangle_{{\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}} \subseteq \hat{V}\otimes_{{\mathbb L}}{{\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}}\\ & 2) \text{ Maximal module}: \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}:=\langle v_{0},...,v_{\mathcal{N}-1}\rangle_{\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}} \subseteq \hat{V}\otimes_{{\mathbb L}}{\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation}$$ ::: We obtain the following. ::: thm **Theorem 4** (Action on quotients of specialised Verma module over the quotient rings). *The generic braid group action $\hat{\rho}_n$ leads to braid group representations on the quotient modules as below: $$1) \ \rho_{\mathcal{N},n} :B_n \rightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_{{\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}} \left( V_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}\right)$$ $$2) \ \widetilde{\rho}_{\mathcal{N},n} :B_n \rightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_{\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}} \left( \widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}\right).$$* ::: 2.5ex -1.5ex Unique quantum traces over quotient rings We want to define knot invariants from quantum traces that are constructed on the endomorphism rings of these modules. First, we will prove that there exists a unique quantum trace associated the level $\mathcal{N}$ maximal module. ::: defn **Definition 5**. A map $\operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}} : \mathrm{End}(\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes (n+1)})\to \mathrm{End}(\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n})$ defined by $$\operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}(f)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \cdots, j_n}} :=\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1} g_j(q, s) \cdot f_{v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n,j}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \cdots, j_n,j}}$$ for some scalars $g_i(s, q)$ is called a "quantum partial trace" if there are two non-zero scalars $a$, $b$ satisfying $$\begin{equation} \operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}(\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\sigma_n\beta_n)) = a \widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\beta_n), \quad \operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}(\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\sigma_n^{-1}\beta_n) ) = a^{-1} \widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\beta_n) \end{equation}$$ for any braid $\beta_n \in B_n$ (see also Notation [14](#endcoeff){reference-type="ref" reference="endcoeff"}). ::: ::: thm **Theorem 6** (Construction of a unique quantum trace over quotient rings). *There exists a unique quantum trace, up to a scalar, defined on the tensor powers of the maximal module (Theorem [29](#thm:uqtr1){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:uqtr1"}): $$\operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}:\operatorname{End}(\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes (n+1)})\rightarrow \operatorname{End}(\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}),$$ where $g_j(q, s) = g_0(q, s) q^{-2j}$ for some non-zero $g_0(q, s)$.* ::: 2.5ex -1.5ex Level $\mathcal{N}$ invariants in quotient rings We are going to use the above quantum trace, in order to introduce the level $\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant of knots. Let ${g_0}(q, s) = s^{-(\mathcal{N}-1)}q^{(\mathcal{N}-1)}$ and $$\operatorname{qt}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}}:=\operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}} \circ \operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes 2}} \circ \cdots \circ \operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes(n-1)}} : \operatorname{End}(\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n})\rightarrow \operatorname{End}(\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}).$$ Let $K$ be a knot and $\beta_n$ is a $n$ braid whose closure is isotopic to $K$. According to the standard argument to construct a knot invariant from the quantum $R$ matrix, $\operatorname{qt}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}}(\rho_{\mathcal{N}, n}(\beta_n))$ is a scalar matrix, and this scalar normalized by the writhe gives a knot invariant. ::: defn **Definition 7** (Level $\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant). Let $$\begin{equation} \widetilde\Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(\beta_n)(q,s) := s^{w(\beta_n)(\mathcal{N}-1)}q^{-w(\beta_n){\mathcal{N}(\mathcal{N}-1)}} \cdot \operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}}\left( \rho_{\mathcal{N},n} \right)_{v_0}^{v_0} \in \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}. \end{equation}$$ ::: Our main result is that $\widetilde\Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(\beta_n)(q,s)$ is a universal knot invariant coming from the level $\mathcal{N}$ representations of $U_q(sl_2)$. ::: {#thm:THEOREM .thm} **Theorem 8** (**Level $\mathcal{N}$ maximal universal invariant**). *For any $\mathcal{N}\in \mathbb N$, $\mathcal{N}\geqslant 2$, $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ is the largest quotient of the polynomial ring $\mathbb L$ with the property that the image of the quantum trace in this quotient gives a knot invariant.* *More precisely, the image of the level $\mathcal{N}$ quantum trace in this quotient ring $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \in \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ is a knot invariant. Also, if $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}'$ is a quotient of ${\mathbb L}$ in which $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\mathcal{N}}(\beta_n)$ is a knot invariant, then the quotient onto $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}'$ factors through $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$.* ::: If $\mathcal{N}$ is a prime integer, then $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}} = {\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}$ and this theorem implies the following. ::: {#coro:prime .coro} **Corollary 9** (**Level $\mathcal{N}$ maximal unified invariant at prime parameters**). *If $\mathcal{N}\in \mathbb N$ is prime, the ring $\mathbb L_{\mathcal{N}}$ is the largest quotient of the polynomial ring ${\mathbb L}$ with the property that the image of the quantum trace in this quotient gives a knot invariant.* *More precisely, for any $\mathcal{N}\in \mathcal{N}$, $\mathcal{N}\geqslant 2$ we have that $$\Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) = \pi_{\mathcal{N}}(\widetilde{\Omega}_{\mathcal{N}}(\beta_n)) \in {\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}$$ is a well-defined oriented knot invariant. Also, if $\mathcal{N}$ prime and we consider ${\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}'$ a quotient of ${\mathbb L}$ in which $\Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(\beta_n)$ is a knot invariant, then the quotient onto ${\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}'$ factors through ${\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}$.* ::: Our next result aims to answer the question about the nature of the two invariants that we constructed so far. 2.5ex -1.5ex Universal versus unified invariants In subsection [\[rec\]](#rec){reference-type="ref" reference="rec"} we study relations between these invariants, and we show in Theorem [39](#JA3){reference-type="ref" reference="JA3"} that the level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant recovers the level $\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant. Then in Theorem [37](#JA1){reference-type="ref" reference="JA1"} and Theorem [39](#JA3){reference-type="ref" reference="JA3"} we show that both level $\mathcal{N}$ universal and unified invariant specialise to the $\mathcal{N}^{th}$ coloured Jones and ADO polynomials by change of coefficients. Then, we show that for any $\mathcal{N}$ (not necessary a prime number) the level $\mathcal{N}$ invariant $\Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$ is an interpolation between the coloured Jones and ADO invariants at level $\mathcal{N}$, as below. ::: {#TINT .thm} **Theorem 10** (**Level $\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant interpolates coloured Jones and ADO invariants**). *We have that $\Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \in {\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}$ is a well defined oriented knot invariant and globalises the $\mathcal{N}^{th}$ coloured Jones and coloured Alexander invariants, as follows: $$\begin{equation} \Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) = J_{\mathcal{N}}(L, q) + \Phi_{\mathcal{N}}(L, s) - \Phi_{\mathcal{N}}(L, q^{1-\mathcal N}). \end{equation}$$* ::: As we have seen above, the level $\mathcal{N}$ invariant $\Omega_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \in {\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}$ has a clear structure, providing a globalisation that interpolates coloured Jones and ADO invariants at level $\mathcal{N}$. ::: rmk **Remark 11** (Rich structure of the level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant). The level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \in \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ has a richer structure, belonging to maximal ring which surjects onto the interpolation ring. We have well-defined specialisation maps from $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ to the rings where the $\mathcal{N}^{th}$ coloured Jones and ADO invariants belong, so $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$ recovers $J_{\mathcal{N}}(L)$ and $\Phi_{\mathcal{N}}(L)$ by specialisation of coefficients. On the other hand, the maximal ring $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ is given by the ideal $$\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_\mathcal{N}=\left( \varphi_\mathcal{N}(q^2) \cdot (s^2 q^{-2\mathcal{N}+2} - 1)\right) \cap \prod_{\text{\scriptsize$\begin{matrix} d\mid \mathcal{N}\\ d \neq 1, \mathcal{N}\end{matrix}$}}\left(\varphi_d(q^2), \frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1} \right) \subseteq \mathbb L.$$ If we fix $d \mid \mathcal{N}$, the presence of the ideal $$\left(\varphi_d(q^2), \frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1}\right)$$ suggests that $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s)$ is related to ADO invariants at level $d$ and an invariant arising from Verma modules at the highest weight parameter being the $d^{th}$ root of unity. This shows that this $d$-part of the ideal, generated by both terms $\varphi_\mathcal{N}(q^2)$ and $\frac{s^{2d}-1}{s^2-1}$ has a rich structure which in turn suggests that the invariant itself could encode deeper information than the sequence of coloured Jones and ADO invariants at levels that divide $\mathcal{N}$. ::: 2.5ex -1.5ex Further directions 2.5ex -1.5ex Structure of the level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant We would like to study the form of the maximal ring at non-prime levels $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$ and the information encoded in the maximal level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant at $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\mathcal{N}}(L)(q,s) \in \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$. 2.5ex -1.5ex Geometrical Level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant In [@Cr2], [@Cr1] the author constructed universal knot invariants and unifications of coloured Jones and ADO polynomials using topological tools, based on configuration spaces in the punctured disc. The level $\mathcal{N}$ universal and level $\mathcal{N}$ unified invariant should have purely topological counterparts in that context, given by Lagrangian intersections in configuration spaces. We are planning to investigate such models for our future research. 2.5ex -1.5ex Level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariants for $3$-manifolds This direction concerns the lift of the level $\mathcal{N}$ universal knot invariants to invariants for $3$-manifolds. Coloured Jones and ADO knot invariants are building blocks for the Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants ([@Witt], [@RT]) and the Costantino-Geer-Patureau invariant ([@BCGP]) respectively. [j]_q!}.$$ ::: {#N:spec .notation} **Notation 12**. (Specialisation of coefficients)\ Let us consider two rings $R,S$ and a free $R$-module $M$. We suppose that we have a fixed basis $\mathscr B$ of $M$. We suppose that we have a specialisation of coefficients that is given by a ring morphism: $\psi: R \rightarrow S.$ Then, we define the specialisation of $M$ by the change of the coefficients $\psi$ as the following $S$-module: $$M|_{\psi}:=M \otimes_{R} S$$ which has the corresponding basis given by $$\mathscr B_{M|_{\psi}}:=\mathscr B \otimes_{R}1 \in M|_{\psi}.$$ ::: ::: notation **Notation 13** (Rings and quotient rings). (Endomorphism coefficients) Let us consider a set of indices $$i_1,...,i_{n} \in \{ 0, \cdots, \mathcal{N}-1\}.$$ We define the associated vector: $$v_{i_1,...,i_n}:=v_{i_1}\otimes \cdots v_{i_n} \in \widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}.$$ Also, for an endomorphism $f \in \operatorname{End}(V_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n})$ we denote by: $$\begin{equation} f_{v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \cdots, j_n}}:=\operatorname{Coeff}(v_{j_1,j_2, \cdots, j_n}, f(v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n})). \end{equation}$$ Here, for a fixed basis of a module $V_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}$ and two basis vectors $v$, $w$ we denote by $$\operatorname{Coeff}(v,w)$$ the coefficient of the vector $v$ in the decomposition of $w$ with respect to the fixed basis. ::: 2.5ex -1.5ex Verma module of $U_q(sl_2)$[]{#2 label="2"} Let us fix $q, s$ to be parameters and in the next part we are going to work over the ring ${\mathbb L}$. We will use the version of the quantum group $U_q(sl_2)$ with divided powers, as presented in [@JK]. ::: defn **Definition 15** (Quantum group over two variables). Let $U_q(sl_2)$ be the algebra over ${\mathbb L}$ that is generated by the sequence of elements $\{ E,\, F^{(n)}, \,K^{\pm1} \mid n \in \mathbb N\}$ subject to the following relations: $$\begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} &KK^{-1}=K^{-1}K=1; \ \ \ KE=q^2EK; \ \ \ KF^{(n)}=q^{-2n} F^{(n)}K;\\ &F^{(n)}F^{(m)}= {n+m \brack n}_{q} F^{(n+m)};\\ &[E,F^{(n+1)}]=F^{(n)}(q^{-n}K-q^{n}K^{-1}). \end{aligned} \end{equation*}$$ ::: Then $U_q(sl_2)$ has a structure of a Hopf algebra (as in [@JK]). ::: defn **Definition 16** (Verma module). We define $\hat{V}$ to be the ${\mathbb L}$-module that is generated by a sequence of vectors that we denote as $\{v_0, v_1,...\}$. Then, we consider the following $U_q(sl_2)$ action on this module $\hat{V}$ (see [@JK]): $$\begin{equation*} %\label{action} \begin{cases} Kv_i=sq^{-2i}v_i,\\ Ev_i=v_{i-1},\\ \displaystyle F^{(n)}v_i = {n+i \brack i}_q \prod _{k=0}^{n-1} (sq^{-k-i}-s^{-1} q^{k+i}) v_{i+n}. \end{cases} \end{equation*}$$ ::: Further, using the structure of the Hopf algebra, we have a braiding that leads to the following $R$-matrix. ::: {#R:R .prop} **Proposition 17** (Generic R-matrix action ([@JK])). *We have the following action on the basis of the tensor power $\hat{V}\otimes \hat{V}$: $$\begin{equation} \label{eq:Rpositive} R(v_i\otimes v_j)= s^{-(i+j)} \sum_{n=0}^{i} q^{2(i-n)(j+n)}q^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}} {n+j \brack j}_q \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \ v_{j+n}\otimes v_{i-n} \end{equation}$$ $$\begin{equation} \label{eq:Rnegative} R^{-1}(v_i\otimes v_j)= s^{(i+j)} \sum_{n=0}^{j} (-1)^{n}q^{-2ij}q^{-\frac{n(n-1)}{2}} {n+i \brack i}_q \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-i-k}-s^{-1}q^{k+i}) \ v_{j-n}\otimes v_{i+n}. \end{equation}$$ Then, this will lead to a braid group representation, which we denote as follows: $$\begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \hat{\rho}_n: B_n \rightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_{U_q(sl_2)}\left(\hat{V}^{\otimes n}\right), \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \sigma _i^{\pm 1}\mapsto Id_V^{\otimes (i-1)}\otimes R^{\pm 1} \otimes Id_V^{\otimes (n-i-1)}. \end{aligned} \label{eq:action} \end{equation}$$* ::: 2.5ex 1.5ex Maximal quotient rings In this section, we introduce various expressions of the ideal $\widetilde\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{N}}$ in ${\mathbb L}$ to define the maximal quotient ring $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$. 2.5ex -1.5ex Defining ideals ::: {#def:condition .defn} **Definition 18** (Condition ideal). Let us consider the following ideals in $\mathbb L$: $$\begin{equation*} \mathcal{J}_{\mathcal{N},k}:=\left( \varphi_k(q^2),\ \ \prod_{i=0}^{k-2}(s^2q^{-2i}-1) \right) \end{equation*}$$ for $k| \mathcal{N}$, $k \neq 1$, $2$, $\mathcal{N}-1$, $\mathcal{N}$ where $\varphi_k$ is the $k^{th}$ cyclotomic polynomial, and $$\begin{equation*} \widetilde{\mathcal{J}}_\mathcal{N}= \mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}\cap\!\!\!\! \bigcap_{\text{\scriptsize$\begin{matrix} d | \mathcal{N}\\[-1pt] d\neq 1, \mathcal{N} \end{matrix}$}} \mathcal{J}_{\mathcal{N},d}, \end{equation*}$$ where $\mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}= \Big( \varphi_\mathcal{N}(q^2)\cdot (s^2q^{-2\mathcal{N}+2}-1) \Big)$ given by [\[qideal\]](#qideal){reference-type="eqref" reference="qideal"}. We call $\widetilde{\mathcal{J}}_\mathcal{N}$ the "condition ideal". ::: ::: {#def:maximal .defn} **Definition 19** (Maximal quotient ideal). Let us consider as well the ideal $$\begin{equation} \label{idealb} \mathcal{C}_\mathcal{N}= \sum_{\substack{i,j=0 \\ j+n\geqslant\mathcal{N},0\leqslant n\leqslant i}}^{\mathcal{N}-1} \left( {n+j \brack j}_q \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \right) \subseteq \mathbb L_{\mathcal{N}} \end{equation}$$ and call it the "maximal quotient ideal". ::: 2.5ex -1.5ex Coincidence of defining ideals We show that the three ideals $\widetilde{\mathcal{J}}_{\mathcal{N}}$, $\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{N}}$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_\mathcal{N}$ are equal. ::: {#prop:EQ .prop} **Proposition 20** (Structural inclusion of condition ideals). *The above three mentioned structural ideals coincide and they also coincide with $\widetilde\mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}$, i.e. $$\begin{equation} \label{eq:EQ} \mathcal{C}_\mathcal{N}= \widetilde{\mathcal{J}}_{\mathcal{N}} = \widetilde\mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}. \end{equation}$$* ::: The proof of this proposition is given in Appendix [\[Ap\]](#Ap){reference-type="ref" reference="Ap"}. ::: coro **Corollary 21**. *If $\mathcal{N}$ is prime, then $$\begin{equation} \label{eq:EQp} \mathcal{C}_\mathcal{N}= \widetilde{\mathcal{J}}_{\mathcal{N}} = \widetilde\mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}= \mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}. \end{equation}$$* ::: ::: rmk **Remark 22**. The equality [\[eq:EQ\]](#eq:EQ){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:EQ"} holds when working over rational coefficients, this is not true if the ground ring is $\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm1}, s^{\pm1}]$ instead of $\mathbb L=\mathbb{Q}[q^{\pm1}, s^{\pm1}]$. On the other hand, the equality [\[eq:EQp\]](#eq:EQp){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:EQp"} also holds over the ground ring $\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm1}, s^{\pm1}]$. ::: 2.5ex -1.5ex Maximal quotient ring at level $\mathcal{N}$ ::: {#def:ring .defn} **Definition 23** (Quotient ring at non prime levels). Let us consider the following quotient ring, and call it "maximal quotient ring": $$\begin{equation*} \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}=\mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \ / {\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_\mathcal{N}}= \mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \ / {\mathcal{C}_\mathcal{N}}. \end{equation*}$$ ::: ::: rmk **Remark 24**. If $\mathcal{N}$ is prime, then $$\widetilde{\mathbb L}_\mathcal{N}= {\mathbb L}_\mathcal{N}= {\mathbb L}/\mathcal{I}_\mathcal{N}.$$ ::: 2.5ex 1.5ex Level $\mathcal{N}$ universal invariant Our aim is to obtain knot invariants at level $\mathcal{N}$, in this case for any natural number $\mathcal{N}$ (not necessary prime as in the previous sections). In the following sections we will see that if $\mathcal{N}$ is not prime, we are able to obtain invariants in rings that are higher than the ring that we have defined for the prime case, which is ${\mathbb L}_{\mathcal{N}}$. In order to do so we are going to use braid group actions on tensor powers of $\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}$. 2.5ex -1.5ex Braid action over the quotient ring[]{#action2 label="action2"} First we will see that the specialised $R$-matrix at these higher rings leads to a well defined action onto $\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}$. ::: prop **Proposition 26** (Action on the higher level $\mathcal{N}$ module over the quotient ring). *The action $\hat{\rho}_n$ given by [\[eq:action\]](#eq:action){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:action"} specialized to the level $\mathcal{N}$ quotient ring $\widetilde{\mathbb L}_\mathcal{N}$ leads to a well defined induced braid group action: $$\widetilde{\rho}_{\mathcal{N},n} :B_n \rightarrow \mathrm{Aut}_{\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}} \left( \widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}\right).$$* ::: ::: proof *Proof.* The condition that we want to prove is that the action $\widetilde{\rho}_{\mathcal{N},n}$ on $\hat{V}\mid_{\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}$ preserves the vector subspace $\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}$. Following the definition of the action $\hat{\rho}_{n}$, it is enough prove that the action of $R$ preserves the vector subspace ${\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes 2}}$. We will show the following property: $$R\mid_{\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}}(v_i\otimes v_j) \in \widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes 2}, \ \ \ \forall i,j \in \{0,...,\mathcal{N}-1\}.$$ Let $i,j \in \{0,...,\mathcal{N}-1\}$. The $R$-matrix action is given by [\[eq:Rpositive\]](#eq:Rpositive){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:Rpositive"} as follows: $$\begin{equation*} R(v_i\otimes v_j)= s^{-(i+j)} \sum_{n=0}^{i} q^{2(i-n)(j+n)}q^{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}} {n+j \brack j}_q \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \ v_{j+n}\otimes v_{i-n}. \end{equation*}$$ We recall that we work over the quotient ring $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}= \mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \ / {\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_\mathcal{N}}$, and this is identified with $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}= \mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \ / {\mathcal{C}_\mathcal{N}}$ using Definition [23](#def:ring){reference-type="ref" reference="def:ring"}. Let us also recall the definition of the ideal $\mathcal{C}_\mathcal{N}$ from relation [\[idealb\]](#idealb){reference-type="eqref" reference="idealb"}: $$\begin{equation*} \mathcal{C}_\mathcal{N}= \sum_{\substack{i,j=0 \\ j+n\geqslant\mathcal{N},0\leqslant n\leqslant i}}^{\mathcal{N}-1} \left( {n+j \brack j}_q \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \right) \subseteq \mathbb L_{\mathcal{N}} \end{equation*}$$ Let $$\widetilde{\pi}: \mathbb L\rightarrow \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}= \mathbb Q[q^{\pm2}, s^{\pm 2}] \ / {\mathcal{C}_\mathcal{N}}.$$ be the canonical projection. We are going to prove that for any indices $i,j \leqslant\mathcal{N}-1 \text { and } j+n\geqslant\mathcal{N}$, we have that: $$\begin{equation*} \widetilde{\pi} \left( {n+j \brack j}_q \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \right)=0 \in \widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}. \end{equation*}$$ This is equivalent to: $$\begin{equation*} {n+j \brack j}_q \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(sq^{-k-j}-s^{-1}q^{k+j}) \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{N}} \end{equation*}$$ if $i,j \leqslant\mathcal{N}-1 \text { and } j+n\geqslant\mathcal{N}$, which holds following the definition of the ideal $\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{N}}$. In turn, this shows that the coefficient of $v_i\otimes v_j$ in $R(v_i\otimes v_j)$ vanishes if $j+n\geqslant\mathcal{N}$. This shows precisely that the action coming from the 2-variable $R$-matrix preserves the module $\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes 2}$ (once specialised to the quotient $\widetilde{{\mathbb L}}_{\mathcal{N}}$) and concludes the proof. ◻ ::: ::: rmk **Remark 27**. Following the above proof we notice that the subset $\left.\left\right|{\widetilde{\mathbb L}_\mathcal{N}}$ of $\hat V\mid_{\widetilde{\mathbb L}_\mathcal{N}}$ is also invariant under the action of the quantum group $U_q(sl_2)$. ::: 2.5ex -1.5ex Unique quantum trace at level $\mathcal{N}$ We recall that our aim is to obtain knot invariants. Now, once we have such an action, we are going to construct a unique quantum trace, which in turn will provide our knot invariants. ::: defn **Definition 28**. A quantum partial trace is a map $$\operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}:\operatorname{End}(\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes (n+1)})\rightarrow \operatorname{End}(\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n})$$ a map which has the form $$\operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}(f)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \cdots, j_n}} :=\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1} g_j(q, s) \cdot f_{v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n,j}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \cdots, j_n,j}}$$ and which satisfies $$\begin{equation} \operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}(\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},{n+1}}(\sigma_n\beta_n)) = a \widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\beta_n), \quad \operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}(\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},{n+1}}(\sigma_n^{-1}\beta_n) ) = a^{-1} \widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\beta_n) \label{eq:qtcondition} \end{equation}$$ for any $\beta_n \in B_n$ and a non-zero element $a \in \widetilde{\mathbb L}_\mathcal{N}$. ::: ::: {#thm:uqtr1 .thm} **Theorem 29** (Unique level $\mathcal{N}$ quantum trace). *There exists a unique quantum trace $\operatorname{qptr}_{V_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}$, up to a scalar multiple, for the level $\mathcal{N}$ sequence of braid group representations $\{\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}\mid n \in \mathbb N\}$. Since the quantum partial trace of $\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\sigma_n^{\pm1}\beta_n)$ is given by $$\begin{multline*} \operatorname{qptr}_{\widetilde{V}_{\mathcal{N}}^{\otimes n}}\left(\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\sigma_n^{\pm1}\beta_n)\right)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n}}^{v_{j_1,j_2, \cdots, j_n}} = \\ =\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \left(\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\sigma_n^{\pm1}\beta_n)\right)_{v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n,j}}^{v_{i_1,i_2, \cdots, i_n,j}} = \\ =\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \cdot \sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1} (id^{\otimes n-1} \otimes R^{\pm1})_{v_{j_1, \cdots, j_{n-1},k,j}}^{v_{j_1, \cdots, j_{n-1},j_n,j}} (\widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\beta_n)\otimes id)_{v_{i_1, \cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n,j}}^{v_{j_1, \cdots, j_{n-1},k,j}} = \\ =\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \cdot \sum_{k=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1} (R^{\pm1})_{k,j}^{v_{j_n,j}} \widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \cdots, j_{n-1},k}} = \\ =\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \cdot (R^{\pm1})_{v_{j_n,j}}^{v_{j_n,j}} \widetilde\rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \cdots, j_{n-1},j_n}} = \\ =\left(\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \cdot (R^{\pm1})_{v_{j_n,j}}^{v_{j_n,j}} \right) \rho_{\mathcal{N},n}(\beta_n)_{v_{i_1, \cdots,i_{n-1}, i_n}}^{v_{j_1, \cdots, j_{n-1},j_n}}, \end{multline*}$$ we only have to show that $\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \cdot (R^{\pm1})_{v_{i,j}}^{v_{i,j}}$ is a non-zero scalar independent of $i$. We see $\sum_{j=0}^{\mathcal{N}-1}g_j(s,q) \cdot R_{v_{i,j}}^{v_{i,j}}$ to show that $g_j(s, q)$ must be $g_0(q,s) q^{-2j}$ by an induction on $M \in \{0,\dots,\mathcal{N}\}$. To show $$\begin{equation*} g_i(q,s)=q^{-2i} \cdot g_0(q,s),\quad \forall \ 0\leqslant i \leqslant M, \end{equation*}$$ we use the fact $$\begin{equation} \sum_{j=0}^{M}q^{-2j} \cdot \left(R_{v_{M,j}}^{v_{M,j}} - R_{v_{M+1,j}}^{v_{M+1,j}}\right) = q^{-2(M+1)}R_{v_{M+1,M+1}}^{v_{M+1,M+1}} \label{eq:sum} \end{equation}$$ given in the following Lemma [31](#lem:qptr){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:qptr"}. \begin{thm}[{\bf Level $\cN$ maximal universal invariant}]\label{thm:THEOREM}
%
For any $\cN \in \N$, $\cN \geq 2$, $\widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}$ is the largest quotient of the polynomial ring $\Liq$ with the property that the image of the quantum trace in this quotient gives a knot invariant. 
\par
More precisely, the image of the level $\cN$ quantum trace in this quotient ring $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\cN}(L)(q,s) \in \widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}$ is a knot invariant. 
Also, if $\widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}'$ is a quotient of $ \Li$ in which $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\cN}(\beta_n)$ is a knot invariant, then the quotient onto $\widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}'$ factors through $\widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}$.
\end{thm}

\begin{thm}[{\bf Level $\cN$ maximal universal invariant}]\label{thm:THEOREM}
%
For any $\cN \in \N$, $\cN \geq 2$, $\widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}$ is the largest quotient of the polynomial ring $\Liq$ with the property that the image of the quantum trace in this quotient gives a knot invariant. 
\par
More precisely, the image of the level $\cN$ quantum trace in this quotient ring $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\cN}(L)(q,s) \in \widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}$ is a knot invariant. 
Also, if $\widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}'$ is a quotient of $ \Li$ in which $\widetilde{\Omega}_{\cN}(\beta_n)$ is a knot invariant, then the quotient onto $\widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}'$ factors through $\widetilde{\Li}_{\cN}$.
\end{thm}
